Subject: RAG evaluation sprint outline & model-fit recs — MediCore Analytics

Hi Sara — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and a proposed evaluation sprint we discussed live so we can move to a short pilot quickly.

Recap of requirements (from your team):
- ~1M document corpus (clinical guidelines, internal SOPs, support tickets).
- Must prioritize factuality and source attribution (PII present in some docs).
- Latency SLO for user-facing answers: ~1s (95th).
- Preference to keep identifiable data in a controlled environment; open to hybrid (index in cloud, sensitive bits on-prem).

Proposed RAG evaluation sprint (3 deliverables):
1) Eval kit: 1k labeled QA pairs (you to provide sample 10k CSV; we attach a small sample).
2) Benchmark harness: automated runs for retrieval+reranking+LM scoring + grounding metrics.
3) Model-fit recommendations and a short pilot (2-week run with metrics).

Initial model & infra recommendations (start small, iterate):
- Retriever embeddings: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (fast) OR redwood-embed-1 (higher recall) depending on vector accuracy needs.
- Candidate LMs for generation (quantized options for cost):
  * Llama-2-13B-chat (q4f16) — good latency/cost balance for closed-domain grounding.
  * Mistral-large-instruct (q4f16) — higher quality on instruction-style prompts in our tests.
  * GPT-J-6B (float) — baseline for speed/throughput comparisons.
- Reranker options: cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 (strong precision) as primary; distilbert-msmarco as a lighter fallback.

Retrieval & chunking recommendations:
- Chunk size: ~400–600 tokens; overlap: 50 tokens.
- Index type: HNSW (ann) with ef_search=128 for interactive loads.
- Retrieval k: 15; rerank top_k: 5–7 (tune for precision@1).

Grounding & quality metrics to track (we'll include these in the harness):
- Precision@1 / Recall@5 (retriever + reranker combined).
- Source attribution rate (fraction of answers that include a verifiable citation).
- Citation precision (are cited sources actually supporting the answer?).
- Hallucination rate (manual eval + automated heuristics).
- Latency (p50/p95) & cost/token.

Attachments included here: small sample CSV (medicore-sample-pack.csv) — please upload full 10k sample to the Drive link below so we can run the harness. Also attaching a short example of our benchmark PDF for reference (redwood-benchmark-results.pdf).

Next steps & owners:
- Sara: upload sample 10k dataset to drive folder by Tue, Mar 28. (MEDICORE)
- Ben: provision dedicated eval capacity + make baseline benchmark run (eta: 48h after dataset available). (REDWOOD)
- Grace: prepare reranker config and evaluation rubric; include manual eval protocol for hallucination checks (eta: Mar 29). (REDWOOD)
- Sean: deliver model-fit doc + meeting to review results (schedule 1hr review the week of Apr 1). (REDWOOD)

Links: Drive eval folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdEXAMPLE-eval-kit
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

If that plan looks good I'll schedule the kickoff and provision the eval cluster.

Thanks — Sean

Sara — great questions, answering inline below.

> 1) PII & hosting: do you expect us to run the retriever/indexing on-prem...?

Short answer: we support both. For the eval: if you can provide a redacted sample we can run the initial pass on hosted eval (faster). For PHI/full-fidelity results we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) so the index and KV caches remain under your network controls. We can run the same harness in your VPC — configuration work is ~1–2 days to mirror the index pipeline.

> 2) Timeline: full 10k QA run (including reranker + manual spot checks)?

Estimate: automated retrieval + reranker + generation for 10k Qs: ~24–36h on a modest dedicated cluster (4xA100 equiv) if we parallelize. Manual spot checks (sampling 200 answers for hallucination/source checks) add ~1–2 business days depending on reviewer headcount; we can provide an outsourced annotation option if you prefer faster turnaround.

> 3) Pricing ballpark: 2-week pilot (hosted) vs. dedicated reserved eval cluster?

Ballpark: hosted eval for short pilot (2 weeks, moderate usage) ~ $8k–$15k depending on token volumes and reranker costs. Dedicated reserved eval cluster (monthly) starts around $35k/mo for the capacity we would provision for repeatable benchmarks (includes cluster, tooling, and 8h/day support). I will pull a formal quote and attach to the HubSpot deal after you confirm preferred path.

Attached: redwood-eval-kit.zip (contains harness, example prompts, scripts to run locally). Drive link above has the runbook.

Can we schedule a 30-min kickoff on Thu, Mar 30 to align owners and confirm which datasets will stay on-prem vs. go to hosted eval? I can do 9–11am PT.

Thanks — Sean
